dedupe_keys.name: quantifying cahoots call data on mobile crisis response and police call diversion eugene oregon dryad

description: This dataset supports a study of CAHOOTS, the longest-running mobile crisis response programme in the United States, which sends unarmed medical and crisis workers instead of police to mental and behavioural health calls in Eugene, Oregon. The authors deposited it on Dryad in September 2026 with a DOI. It holds the call data and code inputs behind a difference-in-differences design that introduces three estimators of how many calls such a programme takes away from police: a substitution diversion rate, estimated at 18 percent, a prevention-adjusted rate of 23 percent, and an overlapping-mandate rate of 50 percent. The deposit is small (about 85 kB) and free to download under a Creative Commons Zero dedication. Caveats: the data describe one city's dispatch records as prepared by the authors, the estimates depend on the study design, and variable definitions should be read in the deposit's README. Simulation uses: calibrating demand splits between police, crisis teams and ambulances in emergency service models, and testing how alternative responders change call volumes and response capacity. Related records: the FCC 911 Master PSAP Registry (data-fcc-911-master-psap-registry) lists the answering points that route such calls and the NFIRS public data (data-usfa-nfirs-public-data-release) describe fire department responses.
